claim: The Calanques are the headline thing to do in Cassis, with ~20km of waymarked footpaths linking Marseille to Cassis and signature experiences like sunrise at En-Vau and swimming at Port-Pin.
quote: The Calanques link Marseille to Cassis along almost 20km of waymarked footpaths. ... Hiking at sunrise in En-Vau, sunset on the Route des Crêtes, swimming in the turquoise waters of Port-Pin.

claim: The park entrance near the Cassis peninsula/Port-Miou is 30 minutes on foot from Cassis town centre; Port-Pin is a further 15 minutes and En-Vau a further 30 minutes, with a steep climb to En-Vau.
quote: just 30 minutes on foot from Cassis town centre ... The Port-Pin calanque is a further 15 minutes, and En-Vau calanque a further 30 minutes ... the climb to En-Vau calanque is steep and can be difficult, particularly in summer.

claim: From Port-Miou it is 2.3 km (30 min) to Port-Pin and 3.8 km (1h15) to En-Vau; the trail is easy to Port-Pin and medium to En-Vau, with slippery rocks on the old seaside GR and a hands-on descent into En-Vau.
quote: To Port Pin: 2,3km (30min) ... To En-vau: 3,8km (1h15) ... Easy until Port Pin / Medium for En-vau ... rocks that are extremely slippery on the part on the sea side in the old GR ... don't hesitate to use your hands.

claim: The classic route starts from Port-Miou on the Cassis peninsula and follows the GR51/98 trail marked in red and white, taking about 1h30 to 2h one way.
quote: The most popular route starts from Port-Miou cove (Cassis peninsula) and follows the GR51/98 trail marked in red and white, taking 1h30 to 2h one way.

claim: The Presqu'île parking sits above Port-Miou (1 Avenue Plage Bleue, 13260 Cassis), free off-season and ~8 euros in high season; the free Gorguettes lot (220 spaces) is a ~30 min walk or served by a free shuttle to Cassis centre and Port-Miou.
quote: The Presqu'île parking is a large shaded parking lot overlooking the calanque ... costs €8 during high season ... located at 1 Avenue Plage Bleue, 13260 Cassis ... The Gorguettes parking lot ... free with 220 spaces, and a free shuttle then serves the center of Cassis and Port-Miou.

claim: From 1 June to 30 September 2026 massif access is governed daily by a prefectural fire-risk decision; on red/black days all trails close and the Route des Crêtes shuts, while only Sugiton (not En-Vau, Port-Miou or Port-Pin) requires a mandatory free reservation on set 2026 dates.
quote: Prohibition to access the Calanques massif (closure of all trails) ... Sugiton requires mandatory free reservation ... Weekends June 20-21 ... Daily June 27 - August 30 ... En-Vau and Cassis-side calanques (Port-Miou, Port-Pin) have NO mandatory reservation systems.

claim: Walking access depends on a prefectoral decision from 1 June to 30 September 2026; walking is usually allowed when wind is low and heat moderate, but any fire risk forbids entry.
quote: Walking regulations depends on a prefectoral decision ... if any risk of fire, the entrance is forbidden.

claim: Les Bateliers de Cassis (GIE) run boat tours at five tiers: 3 calanques (1h, €21), 5 calanques (1h20, €25), 8 calanques (1h50, €29), 9 calanques (2h20, €33), and a 3-calanques-plus-swim-stop (2h, €40).
quote: 3 calanques (1:00h) - €21.00; 5 calanques (1:20h) - €25.00; 8 calanques (1:50h) - €29.00; 9 calanques (2h20) - €33.00; 3 calanques + relaxation stop (2:00h) - €40.00

claim: Standard Bateliers cruises view the cliffs and calanques from the water and do not stop or disembark; only the dedicated relaxation-stop tour includes a swim and is reserved for people who can swim.
quote: The '3 calanques + relaxation stop' tour includes a swimming component and states it is 'reserved for people who know how to swim.'

claim: LOKAYAK, 20m from Grande Mer beach, rents single kayaks in high season (Jun 1-Sep 30) at €30/2h up to €50/6h, two-seaters €45-€85, three-seaters €60-€100; low-season prices are €5 lower; renters must swim 25m unaided and no children under 6.
quote: Single Kayak: 2h €30, 6h €50; Two-Seater: 2h €45, 6h €85; Three-Seater: 2h €60, 6h €100. Low Season prices are €5 lower. Swimmers must complete 25 meters without any assistance; No children under 6 permitted

claim: Destination Calanque offers guided kayak tours from Cassis priced around €47.70 (afternoon), €58.30 (morning) and €74.20 (full day) per person, typically 3 hours, with no children under 12.
quote: guided kayak tours with prices ranging from €47.70 per person for afternoon slots, €58.30 per person for morning slots, and €74.20 per person for full-day tours, with booking fees included

claim: Cassis tourist office lists sea options including soft-propulsion/hybrid eco-labelled boat trips, kayak and paddle (self-guided or guided), snorkelling, and licence-free electric boats; the bay is sheltered by Cap Canaille giving calm, clear water but visitors should check weather, webcams and Calanques access regulations.
quote: Electric boats without a licence for a slow ride at sea... Cap Canaille, the highest maritime cliff in Europe... calm seas, crystal-clear waters... Access regulations: Calanques and Massifs

claim: Licence-free boat rental from Cassis (SamBoat, Click&Boat, JCF Boat, LocBateau) starts around €50/day for small boats up to several hundred euros; small unlicensed boats hold up to 8 people, max 400kg load, and fuel runs about €30/full day, €15/half day paid in cash.
quote: Boats without a license in Cassis start from 372€ per day... some rentals offer boats starting from 50€/day... fuel costs 30€ for a full day and 15€ for a half day... maximum of 8 people and have a maximum load of 400kg

claim: LocBateau rents boats with or without licence by the hour, half-day or full day; unlicensed boats carry up to 8 and licensed boats 8-11, and most of their fleet is authorised to navigate inside the Calanques National Park.
quote: Boats without license: up to 8 people; Boats with license: 8-11 people capacity... most of our boats are authorised to navigate in the Calanques National Park

claim: Plage de la Grande Mer is the main town-center beach near the port, fine sand with gentle-slope clear-water entry, with showers, paid toilets, wheelchair access and a summer lifeguard, and it is the most popular and crowded beach.
quote: Grande-Mer Beach - Surface: Fine sand - Location: Town center, near port and restaurants - Facilities: Showers, toilets (fee), wheelchair access, lifeguard in summer - Crowding: Popular, especially in peak season

claim: Plage de la Grande Mer is a mix of sand and pebbles offering the most amenities including summer-supervised swimming, nearby restaurants and kayak/paddleboard rentals, and gets extremely busy in summer so early morning or late afternoon arrival is best.
quote: Plage de la Grand Mer does get extremely busy in the summer and you are best to either arrive early in the morning or later on in the afternoon ... It's a mix of sand and pebbles and offers the most amenities, including supervised swimming in summer, nearby restaurants, and water sports rentals like kayaks and paddleboards.

claim: TripAdvisor reviewers (4.1/5) describe Plage du Bestouan as a soft pebble beach with lovely clear water and excellent snorkeling (fish, octopus sightings) but say it gets packed in summer heatwaves like a sardine tin, and water can feel freezing in early June.
quote: Lovely clear water, great snorkelling ... so many fish ... packed on a Friday afternoon in a massive heat wave ... sardine bush, high season ... early June brought freezing water

claim: Cassis sea temperature averages about 20.8°C in June and peaks around 22.3°C in August, with the swimming season running June to October and water staying above 20°C through that period.
quote: June: average water temperature 20.8°C ... August has the highest average sea temperature at 22.3°C ... swimming season in Cassis lasts from June to October ... does not drop below 20°C

claim: Cassis village centres on a bustling port with cobbled streets, pastel houses and fountain squares; the tourism office recommends strolling flower-filled alleys, harbour terraces and ice cream while watching the boats.
quote: a village that doesn't cheat ... bustling port, cobbled streets, pastel houses and squares with fountains

claim: The Château de Cassis grew from a 5th-century Roman watch tower, was occupied by the powerful Baux family from 1223, and François des Baux built bulwarks around its four square 8-metre towers and added a Saint-Michel church between 1372-1380.
quote: François des Baux strengthened maritime defenses by building bulwarks around the four square 8-metre high towers. Between 1372–1380, he added a well, baker's oven, and a church dedicated to Saint-Michel.

claim: The Provençal motto attributed to Frédéric Mistral is 'Qu'a vist Paris, se noun a vist Cassis, n'a rèn vist' — 'Who has seen Paris and not Cassis, has not seen anything.'
quote: Qu'a vist Paris, se noun a vist Cassis, n'a rèn vist ... Who has seen Paris and not Cassis, has not seen anything.

claim: Cassis's port is a near-perfect crescent of ochre and pastel facades where café terraces fill by late morning and shaded squares host unhurried games of pétanque.
quote: a near-perfect crescent lined with faded ochre and pastel façades ... Shaded squares become informal gathering places where games of pétanque play out at an unhurried pace.

claim: The Église Saint-Michel in Cassis is a heritage church in the historic centre worth visiting.
quote: Saint Michael's Church (Cassis) | Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur Tourism

claim: The port of Cassis is the centre of daily life, with colourful fishing boats and yachts side by side, fishermen selling their catch by day and dining terraces with sea views by evening.
quote: the port is where a lot of life and history took place ... colourful fishing boats and yachts lie side by side, and fishermen sell their catch during the day while evening terraces fill with people dining with a view of the sea

claim: Cassis was one of the first AOCs in France, established in 1936 when the AOC system was put in place, with each vineyard required to plant at least 60% Marsanne and Clairette; whites are prized as a pairing for bouillabaisse and seafood.
quote: one of the first AOCs in France, established in 1936, when the AOC system was first put in place... each vineyard must be planted with at least 60%... prized not only as a pairing for bouillabaisse but also as delightful aperitif wines and perfect accompaniments for many fish and seafood dishes.

claim: Cassis AOC covers just 215 hectares within the single commune of Cassis, producing roughly one million bottles annually split 67% white, 30% rose and 3% red, from Clairette, Marsanne and Ugni Blanc on limestone terraces beneath Cap Canaille.
quote: The appellation covers just 215 hectares within the single commune of Cassis, producing approximately one million bottles annually, with whites accounting for 67% of production, rosés 30%, and reds only 3%.

claim: The Cassis appellation comprises around 10-12 domaines on 215 hectares, 85% organic or in conversion, sheltered by Cap Canaille (Europe's highest sea cliff at ~400m); the tourism office lists estates including Domaine du Bagnol, Domaine du Paternel and Chateau de Fontcreuse plus tasting venues Divino and La Maison des Vins.
quote: Total Estates: 10 domaines... Vineyard Area: 215 hectares... Organic Status: 85% organic or in conversion... sheltered by Cap Canaille (Europe's highest sea cliff at ~400m)

claim: Clos Sainte Magdeleine farms 12 hectares of organic-certified terraced vineyards on the Cap Canaille cliffs beside the sea; guided tours followed by tasting run April-September Monday-Saturday at 11am and 4pm for groups of 20 at 10 euros per person, with the sales cellar open Tuesday-Saturday.
quote: Clos Sainte Magdeleine works 12 hectares of vineyards on exceptional terraced sites on the cliffs of Cap Canaille and beside the sea... Guided tours of the domain followed by a tasting are organized from April to September for groups of 20 people (from Monday to Saturday, at 11am and at 4pm, €10 per person).

claim: Domaine du Bagnol in Cassis is known for crisp white wines and has a charming wine room where a tasting of 5 different wines costs only 10 euros.
quote: Domaine du Bagnol (Cassis): Known for its crisp white wines. Domaine Du Barnol has a wonderfully charming wine room where the tasting of 5 different wines is only 10€.

claim: The Cassis vineyard is planted exclusively in the district of Cassis, sheltered by Cap Canaille, the tallest coastal cliff in France plunging 400 metres into the Mediterranean, and offers white, rose and red wines with tasting, tours and purchase opportunities.
quote: The Cassis vineyard is planted exclusively in the district of Cassis, sheltered by Cap Canaille, the tallest coastal cliff in France, plunging down from a height of 400 metres into the Mediterranean.

claim: Chateau de Fontcreuse, owned by the Brando family, has made famous Cassis whites since Colonel Teed bought it in 1922; its 38-hectare estate (26 ha in the Cassis AOC) produces a white blend of 60% Marsanne, 15% Clairette and 25% Ugni Blanc and has a tasting room in Cassis.
quote: In 1922, Colonel Teed... bought Chateau Fontcreuse... The Fontcreuse estate covers 38 hectares, 26 of which are in the Cassis appellation... The assemblage of Fontcreuse White Wine is composed of 60% Marsanne, 15% Clairette, 25% Ugni Blanc... the château has a tasting room in Cassis.

claim: Cassis tasting-room standouts include Clos Sainte Magdeleine for stunning sea views and excellent whites and Domaine du Bagnol for crisp whites, with the general advice that visitors should book tours and tastings in advance during peak season.
quote: Clos Sainte Magdeleine... stunning sea views and excellent whites... Domaine du Bagnol... Known for its crisp white wines... Many wineries offer tours and tastings, but it's best to book in advance, especially during peak season.

claim: The Route des Crêtes (D141) is about 17 km between Cassis and La Ciotat, peaking at La Grande Tête at 399m, and features the Pont Naturel arch, the Dent du Chat, and a Semaphore (1791) at 349m.
quote: La Grande Tête – 399m ... Le Pont Naturel, a natural arch carved out by erosion ... Dent du Chat, an astonishing stone arch ... Semaphore, which dates back to 1791 and stands at an altitude of 349m

claim: The D141 along Cap Canaille is roughly 15km long, reaches 394m, has the highest sea cliffs in France, is drivable in 30min (allow 1hr for viewpoints), has free car parks, should be avoided in high wind, and is pedestrianised every Sunday.
quote: the D141 road along the cliffs is about 15 kilometres long ... reach an altitude of 394 metres ... the highest sea cliffs in France ... All car parks are free ... should be avoided when there are high winds ... pedestrianised every Sunday

claim: Cap Canaille is among the highest sea cliffs in Europe; the Route des Crêtes is closed on very windy days, is pedestrian-only every Sunday in season, and parking at viewpoints is limited so arriving early is advised.
quote: at 363m, it is the highest sea cliff in Europe! ... When it's very windy, the road is closed ... from April 28 to September 29, 2024, the Route des Crêtes will be pedestrian-only every Sunday

claim: Cassis SNCF station is 3km from the town centre with a shuttle bus, taxis or a 40-minute walk; trains from Marseille arrive roughly every 30 minutes, and bus 78 links Marseille to Cassis every 45 minutes.
quote: located 3 km from the town centre ... a dedicated shuttle bus, taxis, or a 40-minute walking route ... From Marseille, trains arrive approx. every 30 minutes ... Route 78 connects Marseille to Cassis every 45 minutes

claim: The Relais des Gorguettes is a free 220-space park-and-ride with a free shuttle serving the centre of Cassis and Port-Miou, recommended when central car parks are saturated.
quote: The Gorguettes parking lot is free with 220 spaces, and a free shuttle serves the center of Cassis and Port-Miou

claim: From 1 June to 30 September the Calanques massif is regulated daily by colour-coded fire risk (green/orange/red); on red days land access is banned and the Route des Crêtes is closed, with status updated daily at 6pm and checkable via the 'Mes Calanques' app or by phone.
quote: access bans to the National Park from 1 June to 30 September on days classified as 'red' ... using the official "Mes Calanques" mobile application. The status updates daily at 6pm

claim: Cap Canaille is one of the highest sea cliffs in Europe at 394m at La Grande Tête; the 15km Route des Crêtes can close at any time without notice on windy days, and summer access follows the same massif fire regulations.
quote: one of the highest cliffs in Europe, falling on the sea (394 meters high at the level of the Grande Tête) ... on windy days in particular, the Route des Crêtes can be closed at any time and without notice
